title: Add process-wide semaphore/queue around all bd/dolt subprocess spawns to prevent thread exhaustion
description: Follow-up to nx-t9wlb (nexus-agent crash loop, 31 crashes/23hrs, root-caused to cgroup TasksMax/MemoryMax exhaustion under concurrent bd/dolt subprocess fan-out). Immediate mitigation is bumping TasksMax/MemoryMax in deploy/nexus-agent.service (separate, already dispatched). This is the deeper fix: apps/agent/src/utils/exec.ts (or a shared wrapper) has only a per-call 10s timeout on bd/dolt spawns, no cross-route backpressure -- concurrent hook/route fan-out across sessions (bead-rollup, roadmap-aggregate, beads-unlinked, specs routes) can still spike thread count box-wide even with higher caps. Need a global semaphore/queue bounding total concurrent bd/dolt subprocess spawns regardless of which route triggered them.
notes: Priority raised P2->P1 after independent verification (2026-07-13 17:48): the pthread_create-failed/SIGABRT signature this bead exists to prevent is recurring 141 times/hour in bd/dolt subprocess spawns even AFTER nx-t9wlb's cgroup-limit mitigation (commit 15833a23) -- a HIGHER rate than the original 31-crashes-in-23-hours baseline that mitigation addressed. TasksCurrent=45/1024 at time of failures rules out this specific service's cgroup limit as the active constraint; host free -h shows 15Gi/23Gi swap in use (47 Docker containers also running on this box), suggesting genuine system-wide memory pressure. This bead's fix (bounding concurrent bd/dolt spawns) may reduce nexus-agent's own contribution to that pressure but likely won't fully resolve it alone if the swap pressure is host-wide -- a separate host-level memory/container audit may also be warranted, out of scope for this bead.
close_reason: Shipped: process-wide FIFO semaphore in apps/agent/src/utils/exec.ts bounds concurrent bd/dolt subprocess spawns to BD_DOLT_MAX_CONCURRENT (default 4). Gate applies only to cmd in {bd,dolt}; other exec.ts callers unaffected. Queue wait excluded from the existing 10s ExecTimeoutError budget. Verified: typecheck clean (2 pre-existing unrelated errors confirmed via stash-diff), 11/11 tests pass incl. concurrency-bound + no-starvation + non-gated-unthrottled proof.

title: packages/db missing @types/bun blocks CI typecheck end-to-end (bun:test unresolved)

This is a bigger deal than any individual test-coverage bead: NOTHING in bun test runs in CI right now, PG-gated or not.
close_reason: Fixed in 01398da3 + 19392f97 (pnpm-lock.yaml follow-up): added @types/bun to packages/db, unblocks CI typecheck. Verified: pnpm --filter @nexus/db typecheck exit 0.

title: CI red on main: fresh-DB migration replay broken — duplicate DROP COLUMN value_plaintext (0007 vs 0004)
description: Every main CI run since at least 2026-07-08 fails at the Apply DB schema step: PostgresError column value_plaintext of relation credentials does not exist, code 42703. Verified in run 29174450052 log and in the journal: packages/db/drizzle/0004_encrypt_credentials_finalize.sql line 7 AND 0007_aberrant_silver_fox.sql line 1 both DROP the same column — 0004 appears hand-authored without a snapshot update (meta/0005 + 0006 snapshots still carry the column), so drizzle-kit regenerated the drop as 0007. Any fresh database replay (CI throwaway PG, new dev env, disaster recovery) breaks at 0007; the live homelab DB presumably survived via out-of-band state. Fix is policy-sensitive under migration-only rules: likely IF EXISTS on the 0007 statement or a journal repair — needs its own plan; do NOT hand-edit applied migrations without deciding replay semantics. Masks all downstream CI gates incl. the lint-sql-safety failure (plans/023).
notes: Root cause: 0004_encrypt_credentials_finalize.sql hand-dropped credentials.value_plaintext but drizzle-kit snapshots meta/0004,0005,0006 kept the column, so a later generate re-emitted a redundant DROP COLUMN in 0007. Fresh-DB replay ran 0004 then 0007 -> PostgresError 42703 (undefined_column), red CI on main. Fix (commit aca730ab): (1) removed the value_plaintext column entry from meta/0004,0005,0006 snapshots (0001-0003 correctly retain it, the column existed then); (2) neutralized 0007 to a comment + DROP COLUMN IF EXISTS (already recorded as applied in every env journal, not deleted/renumbered to avoid touching 0008-0048). Verified against a throwaway Postgres 16 (NOT homelab): full 49-migration replay from empty = zero errors, credentials has no value_plaintext + value_encrypted NOT NULL, drizzle-kit generate = No schema changes, drizzle-kit check = Everything's fine, bun test 9 pass 0 fail. Post-push deploy fan-out ran db:migrate on live agents = journal up to date, no pending (confirms 0007 already applied in every env, no re-drop). NOTE: the plans/023 lint-sql-safety gate this bead mentioned was masked by the red replay -- out of scope here; re-triage separately if still red after this fix.
close_reason: Stale drizzle snapshots (0004-0006 kept value_plaintext after 0004's hand-drop) made generate re-emit a redundant DROP in 0007 -> fresh-DB replay 42703. Fixed by correcting the 3 snapshots + neutralizing 0007 to DROP COLUMN IF EXISTS (commit aca730ab). Verified: 49-migration replay from empty on throwaway PG16 = 0 errors, generate No schema changes, check Everything's fine, bun test 9/0.

title: projects table: NULL git_remote_url bypasses unique constraint, unbounded duplicate rows
description: db/project-registry.ts upsertProjectLocations() inserts into projects with .onConflictDoNothing() relying on the (name, git_remote_url) unique constraint. Postgres treats NULL <> NULL, so any discovered repo with no git remote (e.g. a repo with zero remotes configured) never conflicts and gets a brand-new row every discovery cycle (~60s). Confirmed in production: projects table grew to 80,184 rows over 51 days (2026-05-19 to 2026-07-09), 72,900 of them duplicate rows for a single repo with no remote. This also fed a runaway query: the mark-missing step (SELECT id FROM projects WHERE name IN (...) then NOT IN (...)) matched every duplicate, building a multi-thousand-parameter query every minute, logged in full (truncating journald's 48KB line cap) and pegging nexus-agent at 108% CPU for 21+ hours straight before being caught. Cleaned up manually via SQL dedup (80,117 rows deleted, 388 sessions repointed to canonical rows, verified via homelab-postgres/nexus DB 2026-07-09) but the code bug remains and will regrow unbounded for any project with no git remote.
design: Fix needs a NULL-safe uniqueness strategy: either (a) add a partial unique index on projects(name) WHERE git_remote_url IS NULL, and make the insert's onConflictDoNothing target that index explicitly per branch (null vs non-null remote), or (b) normalize gitRemoteUrl to a stable non-null sentinel (e.g. empty string or the local path) before insert so the existing (name, git_remote_url) constraint actually dedupes. Also worth capping/paginating the mark-missing NOT IN query regardless (defense in depth against future large exclusion lists) rather than building one unbounded parameter list per discovery cycle.
close_reason: Fixed in 1c3ebbc6, migration 0049 applied live 2026-07-12 16:14 UTC via db:migrate. Verified post-migration: projects_name_null_remote_unique index present, 0 remaining duplicate groups, sessions.project_id unchanged at 2486 (zero data loss), projects table 7403->141 rows.

title: iOS interact channel
description:
iOS interact channel: keystrokes never reach agent PTY despite client-side send success

CONFIRMED regression/gap in the same bug class mx-rkir.13 was supposed to fix. iOS SshTerminalSession.send() logs 'NXPTY send bytes=N' and calls client.sendInteractiveInput() successfully (no errors), but the owning agent (homelab, single-dashboardEndpoint mode so resolveClient always picks the correct single client) NEVER receives ANY binary interact frame for the session — confirmed via journalctl: zero 'NXPTY interact binary -> pty.write()' AND zero 'NXPTY interact binary DROPPED' log lines despite 15 typed keystrokes AND the automatic resize-triggered Ctrl-L (0x0c) redraw byte (pushResize() in SshTerminalSession.swift:228) in the same window. Writer-claim itself succeeded (agent log: 'NXPTY interact open: writer-claim result claimed:true' at 12:40:45.899, readOnly=false reported client-side). Ground truth confirmed via tmux capture-pane on the actual owning pane (0:2.1) - zero characters landed, prompt line unchanged before/after typing.

REPRO: attach to any live managed session on iOS Simulator (iPhone 17 Pro, iOS 26.5), type on the physical/on-screen keyboard. Agent journalctl (journalctl --user -u nexus-agent) shows the writer-claim but no subsequent binary-frame log lines for that sessionId, for the entire typing window.

SUSPECT AREA: apps/swift/NexusShared/Networking/NexusClient.swift sendInteractiveInput()/openInteract()/PtyInteractChannel - the interactChannel state (private var interactChannel: PtyInteractChannel?) may be getting silently niled or the underlying URLSessionWebSocketTask/NWConnection send call may be silently failing without surfacing to isReadOnly. Need real investigation: add diagnostic logging inside PtyInteractChannel.send() itself (client-side, not just the delegate's SshTerminalSession.send() call site) to confirm whether the WS frame actually transmits over the wire, and check for interactChannel getting reset by a concurrent closeInteract()/openInteract() race (e.g. AttachScene re-mounting, disconnect() firing spuriously, or NavigationStack push/pop lifecycle triggering an extra connect() cycle).

Blocks: openspec/changes/ios-session-navigation task 3.3 (writer-claim + macOS PtyViewer badge-flip verification) - cannot be verified until this is fixed, since keyboard input doesn't reach the PTY at all right now.
notes: ROOT CAUSE (2026-07-13 trace): loss is CLIENT-side in PtyInteractChannel.receiveLoop (NexusClient.swift:1701-1710) — treats ANY non-empty TEXT frame as writer-denial. Agent's interact-open handler calls addViewer(ws) (server-websocket.ts:320-343), which immediately sends the benign geometry TEXT frame (stream-manager.ts:221-227). Client flips isReadOnly=true ms after open AND stops the receive loop; send() (NexusClient.swift:1718-1719) then silently drops every byte with zero logging. Explains all evidence: claimed:true (open ran), zero binary frames incl. auto Ctrl-L (flip precedes pushResize), readOnly=false client report (checked immediately after openInteract, races the geometry frame). The one smoking-gun warning is emitted under hardcoded subsystem dev.leonardoacosta.nexus.mac (NexusClient.swift:19-22) even on iOS — invisible to dev.priceless.nexus log filters. Two more benign TEXT frames also hit interact viewers: source-initiated geometry broadcasts (stream-manager.ts:127-132) and writer_disconnected (stream-manager.ts:251-258), so removing addViewer's frame alone is insufficient. macOS PtyViewer.forwardInput uses the same channel — likely equally broken against current homelab agent (both halves landed same day 2026-05-24: 85cbeb0e interact channel, de27a6b0 geometry frames; the any-text=denial assumption was invalidated in the same batch). FIX: parse text frames in receiveLoop — only type:error (plus close/4009) is a denial; ignore geometry/replay_done/writer_disconnected and KEEP the loop running. Also fix ptyLog hardcoded mac subsystem. Ruled out: agent text/binary mismatch (frame-RECEIVED log fires for every frame kind, zero seen), NWConnection send-before-ready (contentProcessed would log).

close_reason: Fixed: cross-file mock.module contamination. Fixed 10 test files to spread the real barrel or use restorable spyOn+mockRestore (canonical installExecMock/installCoreNodeMock pattern). Test-only, no product change. Full agent suite 26->0 fail (1135 pass/260 skip); pre-push Tier A gate now passes (45s). Merged fb43bbf7.

title: Deploy db:migrate fails on db:push-applied migrations (partial-journal drift; recurring)
description: Every DB batch applies schema via db:push (live-diff, does NOT populate drizzle.__drizzle_migrations). The deploy's 03-migrate runs db:migrate (file replay), which then tries to re-apply the pushed migration and errors (e.g. 0042: 'column vector of fleet_presence already exists', code 42701), aborting the deploy BEFORE the agent restart. migrate.ts has a recovery back-fill but only for the FULLY-EMPTY journal (count=0); it does not handle the partial case (42 of 43 applied) that db:push creates on each batch. Fixes needed: (1) reconcile 0042 now (idempotent re-apply or journal back-fill) so deploys pass; (2) harden migrate.ts recovery to back-fill the missing TAIL when objects already exist (partial drift self-heal); (3) [decision] consider making the deploy use db:push (idempotent live-diff, matches how DB batches apply schema) instead of db:migrate, OR enforce no-db:push-in-batches. Found Phase 1.7 deploy. Agent was manually restarted onto 1.7 (schema already correct via push); only the deploy-migrate journal is broken.
notes:
ARCHITECTURAL DECISION (Leo to choose) — durable fix for the db:push/db:migrate split.

Fix #2 (self-healing migrate.ts, shipped) makes the CURRENT mixed model survivable either way: when a DB batch lands a migration's objects via live-diff and the deploy then file-replays, the replay now records-then-continues on the "already exists" SQLSTATE class (42701/42P07/42710/42P06/42723/42P05) instead of aborting. Genuinely-new migrations (objects absent) still apply normally. So the deploy no longer breaks regardless of which option below is chosen. The decision is about REMOVING the split, not survival.

Option A — deploy uses db:push (drop file-replay entirely):
  - Deploy hook runs `db:push` (drizzle-kit live-diff) instead of `db:migrate`.
  - PRO: matches exactly how every DB batch already applies schema; idempotent by construction; no __drizzle_migrations journal to drift at all; the whole bug class disappears.
  - CON: push is "diff to current schema" — it can silently drop/alter on a bad schema edit, and gives no ordered migration history / no data-migration step. Destructive ops (renames) need care. No audit trail of what ran when.

Option B — forbid db:push in DB batches; rely solely on db:generate + deploy db:migrate:
  - DB batches stop running `pnpm --filter @nexus/db db:push`; schema changes go ONLY through `db:generate` (SQL file) committed to drizzle/, applied at deploy by `db:migrate`.
  - PRO: single ordered source of truth; reviewable SQL; supports data migrations; journal never drifts because nothing else writes the schema.
  - CON: requires discipline (no ad-hoc push during dev batches); slower inner loop; every schema tweak needs a generated migration file + commit.

Recommendation: B is the cleaner long-term model (ordered, reviewable, audit-trailed migrations), but A is lower-friction and matches today's actual workflow. Either is safe now that migrate.ts self-heals. Decision deferred to Leo.

Implementation note: the self-heal reimplements drizzle's own migrate loop (decision is purely max(created_at) < folderMillis, NOT hash matching) with per-statement SAVEPOINT isolation — verified that postgres.js re-raises a caught tx.unsafe() error to the enclosing begin(), so explicit tx.savepoint() is required to swallow the already-exists class without poisoning the transaction.
close_reason: Self-healed partial migration-journal drift. ROOT CAUSE: every DB batch applies schema via db:push (live-diff, writes NO drizzle.__drizzle_migrations rows); deploy 03-migrate runs db:migrate (file replay). drizzle decides what to apply purely by max(created_at) < folderMillis (NOT hash), so after db:push lands migration N's objects the journal is still at N-1 and replay re-runs N -> collision (0042: column vector of fleet_presence already exists, 42701), aborting deploy. RECONCILE: journal was 42 rows / 43 files (0042 unrecorded, schema correct). Hardened db:migrate self-healed 0042 -> journal now 43 (last row hash 95b0b30b... folderMillis 1781963197424, matching what drizzle's own migrator writes). Second immediate run = clean no-op, exit 0 (idempotent). HARDENING: migrate.ts now reimplements drizzle's migrate loop with per-statement SAVEPOINT isolation; catches the already-exists SQLSTATE class (42701/42P07/42710/42P06/42723/42P05), records the migration, and continues; genuinely-new migrations (objects absent) still apply; real errors (e.g. syntax) still abort. 5 new integration tests (real DB, isolated schema) green: partial-heal, idempotent no-op, applies-new, does-not-swallow-real-error, pure isAlreadyExists. bun test packages/db = 7 pass / 0 fail. Agent build unaffected (1265 pass). Architectural decision (A: deploy uses db:push / B: forbid db:push + db:generate-only) recorded in notes for Leo.

title: Writer-reclaim tears down PTY session when 2nd interact client is sole viewer (iPhone takeover regression, af614492)
description: Found greening the Tier A gate. af614492 (ios-session-navigation last-open-wins interact-writer reclaim): when a second interact/writer socket claims the writer role AND it is the only other viewer (no stream viewer attached), claimWriter evicts the prior holder with 4009; the prior socket's Bun close handler fires removeViewer -> viewerCount 0 -> the last-viewer teardown calls endSession() and destroys the PTY BEFORE the new socket's open->addViewer runs -> new client closed with 4004 session-not-found. So the reclaim DESTROYS the session instead of taking it over. This is the iPhone-reclaims-terminal-from-Mac path the feature targets. Probe: c1=4009 c2=4004 viewerCount=0; endSession fires between ws2 claim and ws2 addViewer. Source: server-websocket.ts close handler ~443-459 + open ~316-343; stream-manager.ts claimWriter 264-285. Fix: register new writer/viewer BEFORE evicting prior, OR guard the close-handler endSession against eviction-in-progress. Two tests currently assert against this (websocket-lifecycle + the reject->reclaim rewrite) and both fail — they're the gate's last 2 reds.
close_reason: Fixed in 99111a69: reclaiming-guard set in StreamManager.claimWriter; close handler skips endSession during a writer handoff. Reclaim keeps PTY alive (4009 to old, no 4004 to new); orphan teardown + stream-viewer reclaim preserved. bun test src/ = 997 pass / 0 fail

title: [deploy] macOS banners dead — auto-deploy silently ships ad-hoc unsigned Nexus.app (locked keychain over SSH); team-sign never applies
description: ROOT CAUSE: deploy/lib/macos-swift-deploy.sh:91-114 tries a signed xcodebuild (DEVELOPMENT_TEAM=DX3Y367L2A, CODE_SIGN_STYLE=Automatic) but when run from the post-commit/post-merge git hook over SSH the login keychain is LOCKED -> codesign fails -> script SILENTLY falls back to CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO ad-hoc build (line 103 'falling back to unsigned ad-hoc build'). Installed /Applications/Nexus.app is therefore adhoc/linker-signed, TeamIdentifier=not set, NO entitlements embedded, never registers with Notification Center -> zero macOS banners (TTS audio still works, it needs no auth). Signing identity IS present on Mac ('Apple Development: Leonardo Acosta' valid) + provisioning profiles installed; only the headless keychain lock blocks it. IMMEDIATE FIX: rebuild+install interactively on Mac (unlocked keychain) -> signed app -> grant notification permission. DURABLE FIX (needs Leo decision on keychain pw handling): macos-swift-deploy.sh should 'security unlock-keychain' before the signed build in headless contexts (store pw in 0600 file or dedicated signing keychain), AND the ad-hoc fallback must become LOUD (refuse to overwrite a signed install with ad-hoc, emit a desktop+log warning) so silent degradation can't recur. Ref nx-n2o0a (the team-sign config that the fallback defeats).
notes: FIXED. Mechanism: SSH/git-hook deploy runs in a non-Aqua security session (launchctl managername=Background) where the team identity DX3Y367L2A fails codesign with errSecInternalComponent -> old code silently fell back to ad-hoc (TeamIdentifier=not set, no entitlements, zero banners). New router in deploy/lib/macos-swift-deploy.sh detects non-Aqua and launchctl-kickstarts a GUI LaunchAgent dev.leonardoacosta.nexus.deploy (gui/501, no root, login keychain already unlocked at console), polls a completion marker. The agent runs the SIGNED build inline in the Aqua session. Ad-hoc is now opt-in only (NX_ALLOW_ADHOC=1) and NEVER overwrites a signed install (returns SKIP + desktop banner). PROOF (SSH-triggered path): BEFORE codesign /Applications/Nexus.app = 'adhoc, linker-signed', TeamIdentifier=not set. AFTER = TeamIdentifier=DX3Y367L2A, flags=0x10000(runtime), entitlements embedded (aps-environment=development, app-sandbox, network.client, team-identifier), codesign --verify --strict: valid on disk + satisfies Designated Requirement. Log shows kickstart landed in managername=Aqua, built SIGNED, installed. Interactive auto-mode in Aqua still builds inline+signs (regression OK).
close_reason: SSH-triggered deploy now produces a team-signed (DX3Y367L2A) /Applications/Nexus.app via GUI LaunchAgent kickstart; verified codesign TeamIdentifier=DX3Y367L2A + embedded entitlements + strict verify passes

title: [tts] Question/permission TTS: impersonal 'Permission needed: tool:' + drops all but first question; use full project name
description: FIX LANDS IN ~/dev/cc (cc meta-repo), scripts/hooks/telemetry.sh ~line 1497-1500. (1) jq extracts only .questions[0].question -> multi-question AskUserQuestion drops Q2+ and all options. (2) body hardcoded 'Permission needed: ${tool}: ${detail}'. Leo wants personable: 'Leo, I have some questions regarding <PROJECT FULL NAME>:' then enumerate ALL questions + their answer choices, speakable. Full name: resolve code->name from ~/.claude/scripts/config/projects.json (nx_notify _nx_project_title already reads it; for TTS body strip the icon, use name only e.g. nx->Nexus). Keep generic non-AskUserQuestion permission prompts concise but friendlier. Tracked in nx beads though code is cc-repo.
notes:
Fixed in cc-repo commit ecccb8d1 (github.com/leonardoacosta/central-claude). Files: scripts/hooks/telemetry.sh (permission_request case arm) + scripts/lib/nx-send.sh (new _nx_project_name helper, icon-stripped full name).

Both bugs fixed:
1. AskUserQuestion now iterates .tool_input.questions[] — speaks ALL questions + ALL option labels in order (was .questions[0].question only).
2. Personable phrasing with full project name (nx -> Nexus), not the short code.

title: nexus-agent boots loopback-only when tailscaled wins startup race (Mac notifications dead until restart)
description:
ROOT CAUSE: nexus-agent.service is a systemd --user unit; its After=/Wants=tailscaled.service is a SILENT NO-OP because tailscaled is a system-scope unit (user manager cannot order against system units). On a cold boot, the agent starts before tailscaled completes its handshake. discoverTailscaleIp() retries 5x w/ backoff then falls into degraded mode = loopback-only bind (127.0.0.1:7400 only, no 100.x). Mac listener (Nexus.app SSE observer over Tailscale) can never connect -> ZERO notifications reach the Mac until someone restarts the agent after tailscaled is up.

OBSERVED 2026-06-07: agent booted 07:55:51, log: 'tailscale ip -4 unreachable after retries; binding loopback only (degraded mode)' / 'no current Tailscale IPs; state: NoState'. Only 127.0.0.1:7400 listening. Manual 'systemctl --user restart nexus-agent' -> dual-bind restored (100.73.182.4:7400 + loopback), Mac re-established 5 SSE conns, notifications flow.

DURABLE FIX OPTIONS (pick one):
1. ExecStartPre gate: block until 'tailscale ip -4' succeeds (bounded timeout ~60s) before the agent main starts. Simplest, durable across reboots.
2. Post-boot re-bind watcher: when Tailscale IP appears after degraded boot, bind the Tailscale interface without a full restart (also survives tailscaled restarts).
3. Increase discoverTailscaleIp retry budget substantially (weakest — still racy).

Recommend (1) for the reboot path + (2) for resilience to tailscaled restarts. Band-aid retry in server.ts (nx-ir43a) is insufficient.

FILES: apps/agent/src/server.ts (discoverTailscaleIp/bindServers), deploy/ systemd user unit (the After=tailscaled no-op).
notes: Shipped ExecStartPre Tailscale-readiness gate in deploy/nexus-agent.service (Leo-approved option 1, no re-bind watcher, no .ts changes). Gate blocks until 'tailscale ip -4' resolves, bounded 60s, command -v guard, always exit 0 so Tailscale-less machines still start degraded. Added TimeoutStartSec=120. Rewrote the misleading [Unit] comment: documents that user-unit After=tailscaled.service is a SILENT no-op (user manager cannot order against system unit), the ExecStartPre gate is the durable fix, references bd:nx-j7fmf + bd:nx-ir43a. server.ts retry loop left as-is (residual backstop). Verified: systemd-analyze --user verify exit 0; warm restart -> ss shows dual-bind (100.73.182.4:7400 + 127.0.0.1:7400); journal logs 'tailscale ip -4 ready after 1s — proceeding to dual-bind start' then 'binding agent: loopback + tailscale' (not degraded). Cold-boot race itself requires an actual reboot to fully confirm — not simulable in-session; gate wait-loop logic + clean dual-bind restart are the available evidence.

title: [web-dashboard] take-over release should UNSET window-size (-u) not restore a recorded value
description: On last-viewer disconnect the agent calls restoreGeometry + restoreWindowSize which SETS window-size back to a recorded prior value at window scope (-w) in apps/agent/src/terminal/tmux-pty-source.ts. Leo wants the equivalent of 'tmux set-option -t SESSION -u window-size' on release: UNSET the override so the window inherits global latest and refits to the attached client. This is what fixed his stranded pane live. Likely also a scope bug: resize() pins via -w but the stuck pin was observed at session scope. Fix: on release unset window-size at the correct scope (verify vs live tmux); drop recorded-geometry/prior-value restore; keep a take-over-happened flag so read-only/never-resized disconnects do not touch the pane; update tests.
notes: VERIFIED + SHIPPED. Typecheck (bun run --filter @nexus/agent typecheck) exit 0 — method removals (restoreWindowSize/restoreGeometry/readWindowSizeOption) surfaced no orphaned callers. Affected tests 25/25 PASS: tmux-pty-source.test.ts, tmux-pty-source.integration.test.ts, geometry-takeover.test.ts, commands-resize.test.ts. Assertion coverage confirmed for the new behavior: unit test [1.4] asserts unsetWindowSize() issues set-option -u -t <target> window-size at SESSION scope (no -w), and [1.4] never-resized source is a no-op (zero set-option calls). Integration [2.5] asserts show-options at session scope flips manual then clears on unset. Fixed two pre-existing environmental failures in the integration test (within scope): geometry assertions hardcoded pane rows == window -y, but tmux 3.6a reserves a status-line/pane-border row so pane_height = window_height - 1; relaxed [2.3]/[2.5] to assert source.geometry() round-trips the REAL live pane (exact width, rows within one of requested, never the 80x24 fallback). Unrelated full-suite failures (live-PG integration, execText/execJson) are pre-existing and touch none of the 8 files.
close_reason: Verified: typecheck green, 25/25 affected tests pass, assertion coverage confirms session-scope unset + never-resized no-op. Shipped.

title: [web-dashboard] web terminal does not detach on disconnect — shared pane stuck ~40s at web size
description: When the web client tab-closes/navigates/backgrounds, it does NOT send a clean WS close (only closes on React unmount via TerminalAttach.tsx:432; no pagehide/visibilitychange handler). The agent therefore only detects the dead viewer via pong timeout (PING_INTERVAL_MS=30s + PONG_TIMEOUT_MS=10s = ~40s) before maybeRestoreTakeover reverts the take-over geometry. During that window the shared tmux pane stays at 'window-size manual' = the web client's size, so other viewers (Mac) are stuck shrunken. Fix: client must close both /stream + /interact sockets on pagehide AND visibilitychange->hidden (mobile-correct; beforeunload unreliable). Optional: tighten agent ping interval so ungraceful drops also restore faster. Agent restore path itself works on clean close (server-websocket.ts:403-417).
close_reason: Client now sends a clean WS close on tab-close/navigation via a pagehide listener (TerminalAttach.tsx) that calls the same idempotent client.close() as React unmount, closing BOTH /stream and /interact. Verified with Playwright's native websocket observer: dispatching pagehide closes both sockets (disconnect-restore-verify.spec.ts, green). The agent's existing clean-close restore path (server-websocket.ts close -> maybeRestoreTakeover, apps/agent, out of UI scope) then resizes the shared pane on last-viewer disconnect — no longer waiting out the ~40s pong timeout. Minimal 'resize on close' per Leo; dropped visibilitychange background-detach. Commit 1fa8f8a4. NOT pushed.

title: web terminal renders garbled — overlapping/cramped rows in apps/web attach view (sibling of nx-f1l69)
description: The apps/web @wterm/dom attach view renders a real CC session but the layout is garbled: overlapping/cramped rows, unreadable (see docs/screenshots/img-20260603-065719.png). @wterm/dom/css IS loaded (verified .term-row{height:17px} present in built CSS + linked on the page), so this is NOT missing styles. Likely the web analog of nx-f1l69 (attach-handshake/geometry race): (a) web grid dims mismatch the source tmux pane (agent sends real pane geometry e.g. wide cols; web host can't fit -> catastrophic wrap), (b) autoResize ResizeObserver fights the agent's geometry frames, (c) scrollback seed (capture-pane) fed mid-escape or assumes a different width, (d) cell-size measured before font/CSS settles -> wrong cols/rows. Needs in-browser diagnosis + fix with before/after screenshots.
close_reason: Root cause: autoResize ResizeObserver fought the agent geometry frame (recomputed cols from host px -> grid-vs-VT column mismatch + shared-pane shrink via sendResize). Fix in apps/web/src/components/TerminalAttach.tsx: agent geometry is sole grid authority (autoResize:false, removed onResize->sendResize), fit-to-container by shrinking --term-font-size/--term-row-height (not CSS transform), await fonts.ready before mount, clear _lockHeight. Verified in-browser on live 218-col session: all cols fit, no overlap (rowPitch==rowVisualH), overflowsX=false; typecheck+build green; 4/4 e2e PASS.

title: TTSObserver SSE notification subscription hangs after agent restart (no reconnect)
description: Mac Nexus.app stops receiving NotificationFired entirely after the agent process restarts. Root cause: NexusAggregateClient.consumeNotifications() awaits forever on a half-open SSE connection — when the agent restarts, the Tailscale relay keeps the TCP connection ESTABLISHED so URLSession never sees EOF, consume() never returns, and the nx-gsk4h reconnectLoop never iterates (zero 'reconnecting notifications stream' log lines after restart). Evidence 2026-05-28: agent restarted 13:09 CDT; Mac TTSObserver handler logs stop dead at 12:53 CDT; kernel ACKs probe bytes (TCP-confirmed) but app never surfaces them. Fix direction: add an idle/read timeout (or server keepalive-based liveness watchdog) to the SSE consume so a silent half-open stream forces consume() to return and the reconnect loop fires.
notes: Repro: restart nexus-agent while Nexus.app is running; notifications silently stop until app relaunch. Affects every agent deploy/restart.
close_reason: Fixed — SSE idle watchdog (45s > 30s keepalive) forces reconnect on half-open socket after agent restart. 5 NexusSharedTests pass on Mac.

title: Bug: /events/stream SSE handler closes connection immediately after initial connected event
description:
ROOT CAUSE (verified 2026-04-26):

The /events/stream SSE handler at apps/agent/src/routes/events-sse.ts:93 (handleEventsStream) sends the initial keepalive comment and connected event, then the connection closes within milliseconds. This breaks all downstream consumers including the Mac nexus-notifier daemon.

REPRODUCER (zero-setup):
```bash
curl -sN --no-buffer -v -H "x-nexus-secret: $NEXUS_ATTACH_SECRET" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" http://localhost:7400/events/stream
```

Output:
```
< HTTP/1.1 200 OK
< Content-Type: text/event-stream
< Transfer-Encoding: chunked
: keepalive

data: {"type":"connected","timestamp":"..."}

* transfer closed with outstanding read data remaining
```

EVIDENCE:
- Mac nexus-notifier.sh has logged 15,159 'stream disconnected, reconnecting in 5s' events since 2026-04-24 17:13
- ~16-second cycle: 5s sleep + ~11s connection lifetime
- ~70% of NotificationFired events lost
- Reproducible from localhost (rules out Tailscale/network)
- Reproducible against running binary at ~/.local/bin/nexus-agent (built 2026-04-24 14:03)

UPSTREAM IMPACT:
- TTS notifications from cc/oo/tc/etc. silently lost most of the time
- Architecture comment at apps/agent/src/notifications/channels/tts.ts:18 broken
- 2026-04-26 cc spec migrate-socat-to-nx-notify exposed this — pre-migration the dead UNIX-socket path masked the bug

LIKELY FIX AREAS (apps/agent/src/routes/events-sse.ts):
1. ReadableStream's start() callback may complete synchronously without retaining controller; consider switching to async pull() pattern or explicit controller retention
2. Bun v1.3.11 may have a known SSE/ReadableStream issue with chunked responses — check Bun changelog and known issues
3. Check if any middleware/wrapper between dispatchHandler and the actual response is consuming or closing the stream
4. Verify lifecycleBus.onAny() doesn't throw — if start() throws, controller closes
5. Compare against the WORKING SSE example in spec-events route (apps/agent/src/routes/events-sse.ts also has handleSpecEventsStream which fires 'spec-events SSE client disconnected' — does THAT one work? If yes, diff the two)

CROSS-REF:
- cc-side bead cc-dqmq6 (closed) has full Linux-side verification ladder
- nx-deploy script previously used SSH+nc → now uses nx_notify → POSTs to Linux nexus-agent /notifications/send (works) → fires NotificationFired on lifecycleBus → /events/stream SHOULD push to subscribers (broken)
- Mac listener at /Users/leonardoacosta/bin/nexus-notifier.sh subscribes to /events/stream and pipes 'tts' channel through /usr/bin/say

VERIFICATION (when fix lands):
- Test reproducer above — connection should stay alive past 30s (first keepalive)
- Mac listener disconnect count should drop to ~zero per day (just normal restarts)
- Send 5 nx_notify dispatches in succession; all 5 should produce audio on Mac
close_reason: Fixed in 0195676: set Bun.serve idleTimeout to 255s. Verified end-to-end: Linux agent survives 13s SSE hold, Mac agent survives 13s SSE hold, Mac nexus-notifier zero disconnects in 3+ min (vs 16s cycle before).

title: archive_spec manual-fallback path skips spec-delta merge; openspec CLI ...
description:
archive_spec manual-fallback path skips spec-delta merge; openspec CLI archive can spuriously report 'not found' with exit 0

Reproduced 2026-07-13 during /apply:all wave 1 archive: 'openspec archive fix-interact-text-frame-denial --yes' printed '✖ Error: Change '\''fix-interact-text-frame-denial'\'' not found.' but exited 0. scripts/lib/spec-archive.sh's archive_spec() only guards against two known upstream-bug abort strings ('Validation failed.', 'Aborted. No files were changed.') -- this 'Error: Change ... not found' message does NOT match either pattern, so the function's condition (cli_rc -eq 0 && !grep-match) evaluated true and took the ': # genuine success' branch on the FIRST invocation (spec dir silently left un-archived, zero output). A second, verbose re-invocation of the SAME command somehow then printed the error text and fell through to the manual cp-r+rm-rf fallback (non-deterministic behavior across repeated calls to the same CLI invocation is itself suspicious and unexplained -- possibly an openspec internal index/cache staleness issue on a freshly-created change). The manual fallback path (lines ~99-105 of spec-archive.sh) does a bare directory copy+delete and does NOT run the spec-delta merge step the real 'openspec archive' CLI performs (parsing the change's specs/<capability>/spec.md delta and applying ADDED/MODIFIED requirements into the canonical openspec/specs/<capability>/spec.md). Result: fix-interact-text-frame-denial's two new Requirements ('Interact client text-frame denial discrimination', 'Per-platform interact diagnostics subsystem') were archived but NEVER merged into openspec/specs/terminal-attach/spec.md -- caught only by manually diffing the archived delta file against the live parent spec before reporting completion. Manually merged as a one-off fix this run (commit forthcoming in apply-2026-07-13-002's Phase 6 archive commit). Fix needed: (1) archive_spec's abort-detection guard should treat ANY 'Error:' or '✖' prefixed line in cli_out as a failure signal (not just the two hardcoded strings), not just a success-by-default when the two known strings are absent; (2) the manual fallback branch should either also perform the spec-delta merge (duplicating openspec's merge logic) or, more robustly, hard-fail loudly (non-zero return + explicit ERROR to stdout, not just a stderr WARN) so the orchestrator is forced to notice and manually reconcile specs/ rather than silently completing an archive with a stale parent spec. (3) investigate why the SAME openspec archive invocation behaved differently across two calls -- reproduce and root-cause the apparent CLI-side non-determinism before assuming this was purely a shell-quoting artifact on my end.

title: wave-state wave-complete unconditionally appends to completed_waves ...
description:
wave-state wave-complete unconditionally appends to completed_waves, causing false final-completion on any multi-wave run

cmd_op_wave_complete (scripts/bin/wave-state) does plan.setdefault("completed_waves", []).append(wave_num) with NO dedup check -- unlike cmd_advance_wave, which correctly does 'if current_int not in completed: completed.append(...)'. The documented apply/all.md Phase 3 Step 5 procedure calls BOTH wave-state advance-wave AND wave-state wave-complete --wave N in sequence for every wave. advance-wave already appends wave_num to completed_waves; wave-complete then appends the SAME wave_num again, inflating completed_waves length by 1 extra per wave. For a 2-wave plan, after wave 1 completes: completed_waves=[1,1] (len 2) >= total_waves (2), so wave-complete's 'final = completed_count >= total_waves' check fires prematurely -- plan.status flips to completed, completed_at is stamped, and (when run_id matches RUN_ID_RE) active.txt is deleted + last.txt written, ALL after only wave 1 of 2 actually finished. Reproduced live 2026-07-13 running apply-2026-07-13-002 (fix-interact-text-frame-denial + refocus-board-shell, 2 waves) -- caught before Wave 2 dispatch by inspecting plan state; manually corrected (completed_waves deduped to [1], status reverted to in_progress, completed_at removed, active.txt restored) to continue the run. For a 3+ wave plan the corruption is more insidious: false-final would trigger one wave early rather than immediately, e.g. a 4-wave plan would falsely complete after wave 2 (completed_waves=[1,1,2,2], len 4 >= total_waves 4). Fix: either (a) wave-complete should dedupe like advance-wave (if wave_num not in completed_waves: append), or (b) the apply/all.md Step 5 procedure should stop calling both ops -- pick one authoritative appender. Given advance-wave's docstring says 'Append current_wave to completed_waves (dedup) and increment current_wave by 1' and wave-complete's docstring says 'append to completed_waves, extend completed_specs, advance' they appear to be two independently-evolved paths that were never reconciled to avoid double-counting.

title: Consolidate bead-rollup ready-derivation onto beads-watcher's pure logic (drop bd ready CLI call)
description: bead-rollup.ts computes per-spec/per-project 'ready' task counts by shelling out to 'bd ready --json' (RollupBeadSource.listReady), which (a) defaults to bd's own --limit 10 without passing --limit 0, silently truncating ready counts for any spec/project with >10 ready tasks, and (b) uses bd CLI's ready semantics (excludes in_progress/deferred/hooked) which diverge from beads-watcher.ts's own pure derivation (open non-closed minus blockedIds via deriveBlockedIds). beads-watcher.ts already reuses bead-rollup's deriveBlockedIds/filterUnlinked/collectLinkedBeadIds for blocked+linked semantics but NOT for ready -- it independently derives ready = open-and-not-blocked with zero bd CLI calls. Consolidate: make bead-rollup.ts derive ready the same way (pure, from the already-fetched beads array, no separate bd ready call), so there is exactly one definition of ready shared by both the per-spec rollup surfaces (specs/roadmap/statusline 'N ready' labels) and the per-project unlinked beads-watcher counts. Side benefit: removes one of the two bd subprocess spawns per rollup call, further reducing bd/dolt pthread pressure (complements nx-b6trw's semaphore fix).
close_reason: Shipped: bead-rollup.ts's aggregateRollup now derives ready purely from the fetched bead array (status!=closed && !blocked), identical to beads-watcher.ts's deriveUnlinkedCounts logic. Removed RollupBeadSource.listReady and the bd ready CLI call entirely -- one bd spawn per rollup instead of two, and fixes a latent --limit 10 truncation bug (bd ready was never called with --limit 0). Behavior change pinned by test: in_progress unblocked tasks now count as ready (bd ready CLI excluded them; the shared derivation doesn't). Verified: typecheck clean (2 pre-existing unrelated errors), 41/41 tests pass across bead-rollup/roadmap-aggregate/beads-watcher test files.

Homelab deploy: bun.lock frozen-install drift blocks post-merge hook
description: Post-merge deploy hook (deploy/hooks.d/post-merge/02-deploy) runs 'bun install --frozen-lockfile' before rebuilding nexus-agent. On this machine (homelab) the committed bun.lock no longer matches what 'bun install' resolves — confirmed via a real merge (apply-2026-07-12-002, ff to ed4de0d1): frozen install failed with 'lockfile had changes, but lockfile is frozen', hook logged 'bun install failed; manual recovery required' and continued (non-fatal to git, but nexus-agent did not get a fresh dependency sync). A non-frozen 'bun install' locally produced a 420-line bun.lock diff with ZERO new packages added by the merged commits (verified: neither add-project-status-snapshots nor add-git-status-orbit touched any package.json) -- this is pre-existing drift, likely a bun-version mismatch between whichever machine/bun-version last committed bun.lock and the version now installed here (bun 1.3.11). DB migrations DID apply successfully in the same hook run (2 new migrations, self-healed 0). Needs: (1) confirm which bun version generated the current committed bun.lock, (2) regenerate + commit a fresh bun.lock from a canonical machine/CI, (3) verify the post-merge hook's rebuild step actually restarts nexus-agent with new source even when frozen-install fails, since right now a failure there may leave a stale compiled binary running after a merge.

title: nexus-agent crashed 3x (SIGABRT/SIGILL) under heavy concurrent ...
description:
nexus-agent crashed 3x (SIGABRT/SIGILL) under heavy concurrent multi-session load, memory pinned at 99.9% of 512MB cap

Observed 2026-07-12 12:08-12:10 CDT: nexus-agent.service crashed 3 times in ~2min (status=6/ABRT, status=4/ILL) while ~13 concurrent Claude Code sessions were dispatching parallel bug-fix agents, all hitting bd/dolt heavily (visible bead-rollup ExecTimeoutError warnings for bd ready/bd list timing out at 10s during the same window). MemoryCurrent was 536567808 of MemoryMax=536870912 (99.9%) at time of investigation. No kernel OOM-kill logged, so not a hard OOM -- more likely Bun runtime aborting under severe system-wide resource pressure (thread/process exhaustion) from concurrent subprocess spawning across many sessions, matching the same pthread_create-failed pattern seen elsewhere tonight from a Go-based bd CLI crash. Service self-recovered via systemd Restart= and has been stable/healthy since 12:10:27. Not caused by any of tonight's shipped code changes -- restarts predate the fixes reaching the binary. Worth investigating: (1) whether MemoryMax=512M is too tight for this box's actual concurrent-session load, (2) whether bead-rollup's bd shellouts should back off/queue under contention rather than firing full-speed per project, (3) general capacity planning for how many concurrent Claude sessions this homelab can sustain.
notes: (correction) referenced the wrong bead id in the prior note -- the semaphore follow-up is nx-b6trw (now raised to P1), not nx-dwoqv2 (that id doesn't exist; nx-dwoqv was the unrelated, already-closed credential test-harness bug from earlier this session).

title: nexus-agent: credential usage poller failing 100% — usagePolledAt null on every credential
description: No credential in the /credentials payload has ever been usage-polled on this machine (usagePolledAt null across all entries, verified live 2026-07-11). journalctl history shows 100% poll failure predating the cc-tmux-session-usage-bars deploy. Downstream symptom: 5H and 7D gauges render as dashes in both nexus-statusline and cc-tmux. Root-cause the poller failure (auth? endpoint? schema drift?) and get usage5hUsed/usage5hLimit + 7d fields populating.
notes: Root cause: NOT auth/endpoint -- the HTTP call itself returned 200 OK on every attempt (verified via live debug probe against 3 real primary+available credentials). Bug was schema drift in credential-usage-poller.ts pickWindow(): it only recognized a used/limit response shape, but the real Anthropic oauth-usage payload sends utilization (0-100 percent) with no used/limit fields at all -- every real response was silently rejected as unparseable and counted as a failure. Unrelated to and postdates d36a14f6 (fixed a different bug: pool token-sync gating). Fix: map utilization to used=round(utilization), limit=100, preserving existing integer DB columns and downstream ratio math (proactive-swap.ts, Swift dashboard) -- no migration needed. Verified live: rebuilt binary, found first restart was serving a stale installed binary (systemctl restart alone does not reinstall), fixed via install -m 755, restarted again. Real tick 2026-07-12T01:07:33Z: attempted=15 succeeded=14 failed=1 backedOff=false (up from 0/15 every tick since 15:38). curl localhost:7400/credentials confirms usagePolledAt + usage5hUsed/usage7dUsed populated on 14 rows.
close_reason: Schema drift in parseUsageBody/pickWindow: real API sends utilization-percent not used/limit. Fixed by mapping utilization->used/limit=100. Verified live: real tick 2026-07-12T01:07:33Z succeeded=14/15 (up from 0/15), usagePolledAt populated via curl.

title: iOS AttachScene: PTY sockets do not disconnect on NavigationStack back-pop
notes:
Found during on-device verify of ios-session-navigation task 3.2 (nx-2kxl3), iPhone 17 Pro simulator (iOS 26.5), app pointed at homelab:7400, live session cc-553149-05e2e008 (tmux 0:3.1).

SYMPTOM: After the AttachScene back-button pop, the PTY output stream WebSocket (mode=stream) stays OPEN and ponging for ~3 min post-pop, closing only on app terminate. The interact WS (mode=interact) closes only at its 40.000s pong-timeout (device never pongs the interact channel) — NOT on pop. Neither socket closes promptly when the view is popped.

EVIDENCE (agent journal @ LOG_LEVEL=debug):
- push 09:04:50.254 interact ws:open + claimed:true; 09:04:50.263 stream ws:open
- back tapped 09:05:07, popped 09:05:09 (XCUITest, app held foreground)
- interact ws:close 09:05:30.256 (=40.002s after OPEN = pong-timeout, unrelated to pop)
- stream ws:close 09:07:59 (on app terminate, ~2m50s after pop)
- Ruled out list-stream confound: on the Sessions list with NO attach, no mode=stream opens for the session; the stream is attach-only.

ROOT CAUSE: The sole disconnect path is TerminalHostView.dismantleUIView -> SshTerminalSession.disconnect() (AttachScene.swift:55 comment). It does NOT fire promptly on NavigationStack back-pop. UI task 2.8 / design.md ("Decision: belt-and-suspenders") specified AttachScene should ALSO call disconnect()/closeInteract() on .onDisappear precisely because "a pushed view's teardown timing differs from a sheet's dismantleUIView" — but AttachScene.swift has NO .onDisappear (grep confirms). The predicted risk materialized.

IMPACT: bounded (symmetric writer-reclaim covers the writer-hold; next attach evicts the stale writer via 4009), but a live PTY stream leaks per pop until app suspend/kill, and the writer is held up to 40s. Contradicts task 3.2's "disconnects on pop" clause -> 3.2 left unchecked.

FIX: add .onDisappear { session.disconnect() } (or equivalent) to AttachScene per the original task-2.8 decision. Re-verify stream+interact ws:close fire within ~1-2s of pop.
close_reason: Fixed: added .onDisappear disconnect to AttachScene; re-verified ws:close fires within ~1-2s of back-pop

title: handleSessionStart pid resolution: tmux list-windows -t window-name fails
notes:
Discovered while fixing nx-8kdie (tmux-leak cleanup). The test process-watcher.integration.test.ts "handleSessionStart populates pid, tmuxTarget, cwd" now runs (was 0-tests on HEAD due to afterEach-not-imported) and surfaces a pre-existing PRODUCTION bug.

ROOT CAUSE (fully reproduced, manual, no test code involved):
  apps/agent/src/routes/sessions.ts:314-320 resolves the new window pid via
    tmux list-windows -t <sessionName> -F '#{pane_pid}'
  but <sessionName> is a WINDOW name (created with tmux new-window -n <name>), not a session. tmux -t resolves to a SESSION target, so it fails:
    $ tmux new-window -d -n nexus-int-test-X; tmux list-windows -t nexus-int-test-X -F '#{pane_pid}'
    can't find session: nexus-int-test-X   (exit 1)
  handleSessionStart then logs "tmux list-windows failed; persisting row without pid" and persists pid=0. The test asserts pid>0 -> fails.

IMPACT: every /session/start row is persisted with pid=null/0 in environments where new-window lands in a session whose name != the window name (i.e. always). The process-watcher can't track the PID for these rows.

FIX: target the window correctly, e.g. list-windows -a -F '#{window_name} #{pane_pid}' and match by name, or capture the window id from new-window's -P -F '#{window_id}' and target that. NOT in scope for nx-8kdie (test-hygiene leak); escalated per Scope Explosion rule.
close_reason: Fixed in 3dd948e1: handleSessionStart now captures session:window target atomically via 'tmux new-window -P -F', no more fallible list-windows lookup. Verified: 2 new tests pass, 25 total tests 0 fail.

title: Live-PG session tests seed into shared schema without total teardown (leak project rows, prod-unsafe)
description: sessions.test.ts (seeds sessions + the __nx_sessions_test_alpha__ project) and projects-update.test.ts insert into the shared public schema and run against POSTGRES_URL=prod (localhost:5436/nexus) when NEXUS_PG_TESTS=1. teardown() only deletes the 3 session ids — the seeded PROJECT row leaks even on success; and afterAll-only cleanup leaks all rows on a crash/beforeAll-failure. Fix: migrate these to the isolated throwaway-schema pattern already used by db.test.ts / database.test.ts / process-watcher.test.ts (CREATE SCHEMA <unique> + createDb(url,{connection:{search_path}}) + DROP SCHEMA CASCADE in afterAll) — total failure-safe teardown, never touches prod tables. Also clean the one leaked __nx_sessions_test_alpha__ project + any sessions under it from prod.
close_reason: Migrated sessions.test.ts + projects-update.test.ts to isolated throwaway-schema pattern (apps/agent/src/testing/isolated-pg-schema.ts). Zero-leak proof: before AND after running with NEXUS_PG_TESTS=1, public.sessions(machine=test-machine)=0, public.projects(__nx_sessions_test_alpha__)=0, public.projects(test-project-update)=0, leftover throwaway schemas=0. All seeding/handlers route through the scoped Drizzle handle; teardown is a single DROP SCHEMA CASCADE (tears down sessions+projects+process_watcher_state regardless of outcome). 29 live-PG tests pass; deploy-gate parity 997 pass/243 skip/0 fail with NEXUS_PG_TESTS unset.

title: Capture CC API error text + wire real OTel exporter in agent
description:
Today Nexus sees only the enum tag stop_reason:'api_error' from CC Stop events -- never the actual 'API Error: 500/Overloaded/...' line from the transcript. And OTel is API-ready (@opentelemetry/api + conditional pino transport in packages/core/src/logger.ts) but has NO SDK, NO exporter, and NO span creation in apps/agent. Two gaps to close:

1) ERROR TEXT CAPTURE -- the SessionStopEvent socket schema carries no transcript text. CC hook payload does not include the API Error line. Need a transcript-scraping post-hook (or extend nexus-emit) to extract the last 'API Error:' line, add an error_details field to the socket schema (apps/agent/src/routes/hooks-types.ts), thread it through process-hook-event, persist it, and surface it in the crash notification body (apps/agent/src/notifications/hook-rules.ts -- currently all 5 crash reasons share one generic 'session crashed' body).

2) REAL OTEL -- wire an actual @opentelemetry/sdk + OTLP exporter on agent startup, create spans for socket dispatch / hook processing / DB writes, so an api_error stop can be correlated to a trace. Today the agent is trace-id pass-through only (decorates pino logs + scriptErrors.traceId but owns no span lifecycle).
design: Affected files: apps/agent/src/routes/hooks-types.ts (SessionStopEvent schema), apps/agent/src/services/process-hook-event.ts (enrich), apps/agent/src/notifications/hook-rules.ts (CRASH_STOP_REASONS classification + notification body), packages/core/src/logger.ts (OTel SDK bootstrap), packages/db schema (error_details column). Multi-file + schema + socket-contract change -> needs design review per Design Gate before impl.
acceptance_criteria: (1) An api_error stop event persists the actual 'API Error: XXX' message and the crash notification body includes it. (2) Agent boots an OTel SDK with an OTLP exporter and emits at least one span per hook-event dispatch, correlatable by traceId. (3) Per-reason classification distinguishes api_error from timeout/oom/crash.
notes: DECISIONS (2026-06-16, Leo): (D-B) PART B = full OTel SDK (@opentelemetry/sdk-trace-node + exporter-trace-otlp-http) gated on OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT, ConsoleSpanExporter fallback for dev visibility. (D-A) PART A = persist error_details/stop_reason to sessions row AND revive the dormant notify path (thread NotificationManager into dispatcher so api_error fires a desktop/TTS alert with the error text). (D2) Cross-repo: edit ~/dev/cc telemetry.sh handle_session_stop to scrape last 'API Error:' line and emit error_details on the wire -- separate cc commit. Key finding: sessionStopRule/evaluateAndDispatch are dormant (zero prod callers) -- A8 wiring required. Schema is plain TS interfaces (not Zod) on the socket path. error_details/stop_reason columns go on sessions table (not session_events). Migrate via pnpm --filter @nexus/db db:push.
close_reason: PART A: error_details+stop_reason columns on sessions table (live in PG), SessionStopEvent extended, recordSessionStop writer, dispatcher persists on session_stop, evaluateAndDispatch revived so api_error fires desktop/TTS notification with error text, hook-rules per-reason classification. PART B: otel.ts (sdk-trace-node 2.8.0, OTLP or ConsoleSpanExporter), provider.register(), getTracer export, hook.dispatch span in dispatcher, index.ts first-import. cc telemetry.sh extracts last API Error: line from transcript and emits error_details on the wire. 129 tests pass, bun build 1186 modules, PG integration confirmed. Committed c0d6c592 (nx) and 541d42a1 (cc).

title: [healthkit] Wave 2: homelab APNS silent-push service for periodic health flush
description: Server-driven background wake so health flushes happen on a GUARANTEED cadence (iOS on-device schedulers in Wave 1 are best-effort/throttled). The iOS side is DONE (Wave 1, e306c86c): didReceiveRemoteNotification handles aps content-available:1 + userInfo.nexusKind='health-flush' -> HealthKitPushManager.flushAll(). This issue is the AGENT (TS, port 7400) side.
design:
DEPENDENCY CHAIN (each step gates the next):
1. /apns/register POST endpoint in apps/agent (clone an init*Routes in routes/) + a device_tokens table (db migration, clone db/ helpers). ApnsRegistrar already POSTs {platform,token,bundleId} to NEXUS_ENDPOINT/apns/register -- currently 404s.
2. Rebuild+redeploy nexus-ios so didRegisterForRemoteNotifications captures a SANDBOX token (entitlement aps-environment=development) and stores it.
3. APNs sender module: ES256 JWT signed with AuthKey_Z3BX2Y72Q7.p8 (keyID Z3BX2Y72Q7, teamID DX3Y367L2A), HTTP/2 POST to api.sandbox.push.apple.com/3/device/<token>, headers apns-topic=dev.leonardoacosta.nexus.ios, apns-push-type=background, apns-priority=5, body {aps:{content-available:1},nexusKind:'health-flush'}. VERIFY: a 200 (or 400 BadDeviceToken with a junk token) proves the key authenticates; 403 InvalidProviderToken => wrong key (confirm Z3BX2Y72Q7 is an APNs Auth Key on the portal, not a second ASC key).
4. Periodic timer (clone HealthScheduler setInterval pattern) sending the silent push every ~30-60min to all registered tokens.
VERIFICATION CAVEAT: silent pushes are best-effort + iOS-throttled; observe via device os.log (healthkit-push category) + the resulting mx-health ingest POSTs, not a deterministic per-push assertion.
notes: DIAGNOSIS (foreground-launch test, decisive): force-foregrounding the app landed +18 new samples instantly -> the on-device flush + POST + homelab ingest path WORKS and new data exists. But 2 silent pushes (APNs HTTP 200, app process confirmed running on device) triggered ZERO flush. CONCLUSION: engineering is correct; iOS THROTTLES background content-available pushes (and BGTask) via the per-app background budget -- best-effort by Apple's design, heavily restricted for a low-usage freshly-installed app. APNs 200 = queued, NOT delivered/woken. DECISION (Leo): tune + accept opportunistic -- enable Background App Refresh for Nexus + avoid Low Power Mode; the homelab 30m scheduler + BGTask + foreground-on-open sync opportunistically as iOS grants budget. NOT pursuing Wave 3 (silent-audio keepalive). Wave 2 functionally complete: sender/store/register/scheduler all live + verified server-side; the wake cadence is iOS-limited, not a code defect.
close_reason: Wave 2 built + deployed + server-side-verified (key auths, token captured, push accepted HTTP 200, scheduler running). Background wake is iOS-budget-throttled by design; data path proven via foreground (+18 samples). Leo: tune + accept opportunistic, no Wave 3.

title: [healthkit] iOS HealthKit push module -> homelab mx-health ingest
description: Add an Apple HealthKit READ + push module to the nexus-ios target. Reads resting HR / HR / HRV via HKAnchoredObjectQuery (persisted anchor, incremental), registers HKObserverQuery + background delivery for push-on-change, and POSTs the Health Auto Export JSON shape to the homelab mx-health ingest (http://homelab:8796/ingest) over the tailnet. This is the PRODUCTION producer for mx-sqd/mx-4d0 (mx repo) -- replaces the Health Auto Export stopgap. Direct-to-homelab routing (not via the nexus agent). NOTE: distinct from the existing nx 'health' = system metrics (HealthSummaryScene/HealthCollector); this is Apple biometric HealthKit.
design: Clone ApnsRegistrar actor+endpoint pattern. Endpoint via Info.plist HEALTH_INGEST_ENDPOINT (fallback http://homelab:8796/ingest). Date format yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss Z to match the Go decoder layout 2006-01-02 15:04:05 -0700. Entitlement: com.apple.developer.healthkit + .background-delivery. Apple-portal step: enable HealthKit on nexus_ios_development provisioning profile before a device build. Build/deploy on Mac (Linux cannot xcodebuild).
notes: WAVE 1 COMPLETE + DEPLOYED + PROVEN: all-metrics read (40 distinct types now landing) + chunked backfill (5k/POST) + 3 background wake paths (HKObserverQuery, BGTaskScheduler refresh+processing, silent-push handler). After deploy: 2,219,337 samples in mx_health_samples across 40 metric types incl third-party (WHOOP/Withings/Endel/NapBot). Commits b53df177 + e306c86c on main. WAVE 2 (this issue's remaining scope): homelab APNS silent-push SERVICE so the server guarantees a wake cadence -- APNs key AuthKey_Z3BX2Y72Q7.p8 (keyID Z3BX2Y72Q7, team DX3Y367L2A, bundle dev.leonardoacosta.nexus.ios, DEV build => sandbox APNs api.sandbox.push.apple.com). Components: /apns/register endpoint + device_tokens storage in the agent, ES256 JWT APNs sender, periodic timer sending aps content-available:1 + nexusKind=health-flush. App side already handles it (didReceiveRemoteNotification).

title: Thread custom session name (CC customTitle) into notifications — spoken TTS + banner name the session
description: CC persists the /rename title as customTitle in the session transcript jsonl (mirrored to agentName) but it never reaches nexus — hooks send only session_id, and NotificationEvent has no session linkage. Wire it end-to-end (notifications-first). WIRE CONTRACT: hook payload uses session_name (snake, matches tool_name/hook_event_name); HookEventPayload.session_name?: string; NotificationDraft + NotificationFired lifecycle + NotificationEvent JSON use sessionName (camelCase, matches logPath/audioBase64); Swift NotificationEvent.sessionName: String?. SOURCE: telemetry.sh reads .transcript_path from STDIN_JSON, extracts latest customTitle from that jsonl. Two consumer paths: (1) telemetry.sh nx_notify personable TTS -> 'Leo, I have some questions in your <name> session regarding <Project>:'; (2) NotificationFired -> Swift banner + TTS + Session-sort upgrade (replaces channel proxy). Absent customTitle -> omit gracefully (keep current 'regarding Nexus').
notes: backend wave done (Path A telemetry.sh + Path B nx agent/core). Wire emitted: hook payload session_name (snake); HookEventPayload.session_name?; NotificationDraft.sessionName?; NotificationTransportExtras.sessionName?; NotificationFiredPayload.sessionName? (lifecycle emit); core NotificationEvent.sessionName?. Empty/absent customTitle omits the field (undefined) and degrades to today text. Sample spoken (with name): Leo, I have some questions in your "backend wave" session regarding nexus: <questions>. Tests: 36 pass (hook-rules + hook-trigger + manager-session-name). Typecheck core+agent 0 errors. STILL IN PROGRESS: Swift consumer wave pending.

title: [notifications] Ducking options indistinguishable — Duck only drops TTS player to 90% (wrong direction, imperceptible); Pause-others is a dead no-op on macOS
description: AudioPlayer.swift:43 sets player.volume = ducking == .duck ? 0.9 : 1.0 — Duck lowers OUR TTS to 90% (should lower OTHER audio, and 10% is imperceptible) and .pause falls through to full volume = identical to .mix (dead binding). Leo: 'I dont hear a difference.' macOS has no AVAudioSession.duckOthers; investigate feasible macOS approaches to duck/pause OTHER apps audio (Core Audio default-device volume, MPNowPlaying, or media-key). If true other-app ducking is infeasible on macOS, make the three options at minimum AUDIBLY distinct and remove/relabel the misleading dead option rather than shipping a no-op. Files: NexusShared AudioPlayer.swift, MP3Player.swift (DuckingMode enum), TTSObserver.swift resolveDucking.
close_reason: Shipped in 81b5da11; nexus-mac BUILD SUCCEEDED on Mac (signing-disabled). macOS has no AVAudioSession.duckOthers and no per-app output volume, so AudioPlayer.swift now ducks the SYSTEM output volume via CoreAudio/AudioToolbox AudioHardwareService (kAudioHardwareServiceDeviceProperty_VirtualMainVolume): .mix=no change, .duck=40%, .pause(relabeled 'Quiet')=15%, with save/restore of the pre-duck system volume on finish+stop+supersede. Tradeoff: this lowers the WHOLE system output (not just other apps) for the TTS duration since macOS exposes no per-app volume control — the three modes are now AUDIBLY distinct and the previously-dead .pause option is meaningful. Picker relabeled Pause->Quiet in NotificationsView + SettingsTtsView for parity; MP3Player DuckingMode doc comment updated (enum cases unchanged).

title: TmuxPtySource.write fire-and-forget send-keys reorders fast keystrokes
description: Found during wterm-web-terminal Batch 4 E2E (nx-64r21). apps/agent/src/terminal/tmux-pty-source.ts write() does a fire-and-forget Bun.spawn(['tmux','send-keys','-l',text]) per stdin frame with 'void proc.exited' (no await/queue). The browser interact channel emits one WS binary frame PER keystroke (WTerm.onData), so a fast type burst spawns N concurrent 'tmux send-keys' subprocesses that race -> chars land out of order (observed: 'echo nexus-e2e-X' rendered as 'eco hnexus-ee2-X' -> 'bash: eco: command not found'). Repro: Playwright page.keyboard.type() with 0 delay against /attach/:id. Mitigated in the E2E by pacing keystrokes (delay:75ms). Fix options: (a) serialize writes through an async queue that awaits each send-keys, or (b) coalesce stdin frames in a microtask before a single send-keys. Real-user impact: paste / very fast typing can scramble input.
notes: CONFIRMED still present (verified 2026-07-12): tmux-pty-source.ts:491-515 write() still spawns a new fire-and-forget tmux send-keys subprocess per call with zero await/queue/serialization -- void proc.exited.then(...) is log-only, does not block subsequent writes. The described race (fast keystroke bursts spawn N concurrent send-keys that can interleave/reorder) is unchanged from the original report. Not fixed.
close_reason: Fixed in dff7601d: write() now serializes tmux send-keys via an internal promise queue, still fire-and-forget for callers. Verified: new regression test proves maxConcurrent===1, 15 tests pass across unit+integration.

title: [CAPABILITY] session-persistence
PTY viewer output garbled
description:
PTY viewer output garbled — attach-handshake/geometry race (SwiftTerm setup is correct)

The Mac dashboard PTY viewer shows jumbled/garbled terminal output. Investigation (2026-05-28) ruled OUT the obvious cause: PtyViewer.swift already feeds bytes to a real VT emulator (SwiftTerm, terminal.feed line 538) and the agent streams live raw bytes via tmux pipe-pane (apps/agent/src/terminal/tmux-pty-source.ts:308) — not snapshots. So the renderer is sound; the garble is an attach-handshake / geometry race. Suspected causes: (a) bytes arrive before the initial resize(cols,rows) geometry frame so cursor-positioning escapes land in a wrong-sized grid; (b) the capture-pane -e scrollback seed (tmux-pty-source.ts:179) splits on lines and can hand SwiftTerm a mid-escape-sequence boundary when the live pipe-pane stream takes over; (c) the 1MB pre-attach buffer drop (PtyViewer.swift ~543) truncates mid-sequence. DO NOT rewrite the renderer or switch to tmux control-mode / a headless emulator — that throws away a working SwiftTerm integration.
design: INSTRUMENT FIRST, then fix. Step 1 (spike): add telemetry to the attach path — log geometry-frame timestamp vs first-byte timestamp, the initial grid (cols,rows), and any 1MB buffer-drop events; reproduce the garble and capture which race fires. Step 2 (fix, scope TBD by step 1): guarantee the geometry frame is delivered+applied before the first byte is fed; align the scrollback seed to escape-sequence boundaries; revisit the buffer-drop to avoid mid-sequence truncation.
notes: Instrumentation spike SHIPPED + Mac-compile-verified (commit 7217d2c1): nx-f1l69-tagged logs on both sides of the attach handshake — agent tmux-pty-source.ts (scrollbackSeed endsClean, paneDims ordering, firstData) + Swift PtyViewer.swift (geometry recv/applied, firstFeed geometryApplied, feed midEscape, preAttachDrop/Drain). STILL OPEN — awaiting a repro: on Mac run an attach with log stream --predicate subsystem==dev.priceless.nexus + grep nx-f1l69 on agent pino output; the paired timeline pinpoints cause (a) byte-before-geometry race, (b) scrollback-seed mid-escape boundary, or (c) 1MB buffer-drop mid-escape. Then implement the targeted fix.

title: Banner post fails UNError 1 on ad-hoc-signed Nexus.app despite requestAuthorization
description: CORRECTED root cause: the app DOES request authorization (nexusApp.swift:109, options [.alert,.sound], logs granted result). Banner posts still fail Error Domain=UNErrorDomain Code=1 because /Applications/Nexus.app is AD-HOC signed (codesign: flags=0x20002 adhoc,linker-signed; Signature=adhoc; TeamIdentifier=not set). For ad-hoc binaries macOS notification grants do not reliably persist/associate — System Settings can show Nexus 'Allow Notifications' ON while UNUserNotificationCenter.add() still returns notificationsNotAllowed. Evidence 2026-05-28: ~/Library/Preferences/com.apple.ncprefs.plist last modified Jul 25 2025 (no grant written in ~10mo); 40+ 'banner post failed UNError Code=1' 11:08-12:53 CDT. NOTE: this gates the VISUAL BANNER ONLY — audio is independent (nexusApp.swift:106-108). Fix direction: sign nexus-mac with a stable Developer ID (or persistent self-signed identity) so the notification authorization persists across launches/rebuilds; optionally surface a denied/notDetermined warning at startup like warnIfSystemOutputMuted.
notes: FIX APPLIED + config-verified (commit 1b0e35ab): DEVELOPMENT_TEAM corrected to DX3Y367L2A (the cert OU; the (4RMU5SA5Z4) in the cert CN is an Apple-ID suffix, NOT the team). Signed build on Mac now RESOLVES the correct identity (Apple Development: Leonardo Acosta, sha1 8E126B18) + the existing 'Mac Team Provisioning Profile: dev.leonardoacosta.nexus.mac' (carries aps-environment + iCloud, expires 2027) — the prior 'No Account'/'No profiles' errors are gone. Remaining: the actual codesign step fails over ssh with errSecInternalComponent (non-interactive session can't use the locked login-keychain private key) — this is a remote-build artifact, NOT a config problem. FINAL VERIFY (Leo, in GUI session): build nexus-mac in Xcode (or any build from the logged-in desktop), then run: codesign -dvvv /Applications/Nexus.app 2>&1 | grep TeamIdentifier  → expect TeamIdentifier=DX3Y367L2A (not adhoc). Then notification authorization persists and banners post. Close when confirmed.

title: [PROPOSAL] add-hooks-sse-fanout
description:
Re-emit persisted hook events to /events/stream so the Next.js dashboard updates live without polling.

Today, /events/stream broadcasts lifecycleBus events (NotificationFired, SessionStarted, SettingsChanged-future). Hook events that landed in session_events are NOT broadcast, so dashboards must poll /sessions or /failures to see new activity.

Scope:
- After session_events insert in handleHooks, emit a lifecycleBus event (e.g. HookEventReceived with {event_type, session_id, project, event_id}).
- SSE subscribers (apps/nextjs dashboard pages) filter by event_type to refresh their views.
- /session/[id] page uses the stream to live-append a session timeline.
- /projects/[name] uses it to update session-count badges.
- Optional throttle: high-frequency events (tool_use_end on tight loops) batched at 500ms intervals.

Depends on: extend-hooks-event-taxonomy (broadcasting events that don't exist yet is hollow).
Sibling: add-hooks-notification-triggers (independent — both react to recognized events).
Predecessor: restore-hooks-event-persistence (archived 2026-04-27).

title: [PROPOSAL] add-hooks-notification-triggers
description:
Wire selected hook events into the notification pipeline so high-signal CC events surface as desktop/TTS/Slack notifications.

Trigger events (per CC's curated routing policy in telemetry.sh):
- tool_use_fail → desktop + (optionally) Slack
- permission_request → desktop + TTS (interactive — user wants prompt audibility)
- hook_failure → desktop + Slack
- session_stop with crash flag → desktop + Slack
- session_summary on long sessions (cost > threshold) → optional digest

Routing should reuse the existing notification-router rule engine (apps/agent/src/notifications/router.ts). Each event type maps to a small declarative rule with channel set + suppression heuristics (dedupe by tool_name within N seconds, etc.).

Scope:
- Map of event_type → notification template + channels (project-prefixed body).
- Dedupe / coalesce strategy for noisy events (tool_use_fail in tight retry loops).
- Respect notification_settings (when add-notification-control-dashboard ships).
- Tests for each rule firing exactly once per qualifying event.

Depends on: extend-hooks-event-taxonomy (events must be recognized + parsed before they can trigger notifications).
Sibling: add-hooks-sse-fanout (dashboard tail).

title: Mac nexus-notifier TTS playback overlaps when notifications burst
description:
OBSERVED: When two or more notifications fire within a few seconds, the Mac nexus-notifier launches concurrent backgrounded `say` processes that play simultaneously.

ROOT CAUSE: ~/bin/nexus-notifier.sh _dispatch_tts runs `/usr/bin/say -- "$body" &` — trailing & detaches each say as independent process. No serialization.

PRIOR ART: Nova (~/dev/nv/packages/daemon/src/features/tts/) has a serial queue: single worker owns audio output, requests append to FIFO, worker drains serially.

FIX OPTIONS for nexus-notifier.sh:
  (A) flock-based mutex around `say` — simplest, blocks SSE loop while playing
  (B) Named-pipe queue + drain worker — preferred, non-blocking dispatch with serial playback
  (C) Dedicated launchctl playback service — over-engineered

REPRO: for i in 1 2 3; do nx_notify "Burst test $i"; done — three voices overlap.

ACCEPTANCE:
  - 5 burst nx_notify calls produce 5 sequential utterances
  - SSE listener does not drop events while audio plays
  - Recommend Shape B

title: Mac nexus-notifier TTS playback overlaps when notifications burst
description:
OBSERVED: When two or more notifications fire within a few seconds (common during multi-agent batch operations), the Mac nexus-notifier launches concurrent backgrounded `say` processes that play simultaneously and step on each other.

ROOT CAUSE (verified): In ~/bin/nexus-notifier.sh the _dispatch_tts handler does:

  /usr/bin/say -- "$body" 2>>"$LOG_FILE" &

The trailing & detaches each say invocation as an independent process. There is no serialization, queue, or wait-for-previous mechanism. So a burst of N notifications spawns N concurrent say processes.

PRIOR ART: Nova (~/dev/nv/packages/daemon/src/features/tts/) implements a serial playback queue. Pattern to borrow:
  1. A single playback worker process owns the audio output
  2. Incoming TTS requests append to a queue (file, FIFO, or in-memory)
  3. Worker drains the queue serially: play current item, wait for completion, dequeue next

LIGHTWEIGHT FIX OPTIONS for nexus-notifier.sh (single bash script):
  (A) flock-based mutex around `say` — guarantees no overlap, simplest, blocks the SSE-read loop while playing (a few seconds per notification)
  (B) Named-pipe queue: spawn a single drain worker on script start that reads lines from a FIFO and runs `say` synchronously. Producer (the dispatch handler) just echoes to the FIFO.
  (C) launchctl-managed dedicated playback service that subscribes to a separate event topic — over-engineered for our use case

REPRODUCER:
  source ~/.claude/scripts/lib/nx-send.sh
  for i in 1 2 3; do nx_notify "Burst test message number $i, listen for overlap"; done

EXPECTED: Three sequential utterances played one after another.
ACTUAL: Three voices speaking over each other.

ACCEPTANCE:
  - Burst of 5 nx_notify calls produces 5 sequential, non-overlapping utterances
  - Listener does not lose SSE events while playing (so dispatch must be non-blocking even if playback is serial)
  - Recommendation B (named-pipe + drain worker) preferred for the non-blocking dispatch property

REFERENCE:
  - Nova prior art: ~/dev/nv/packages/daemon/src/features/tts/
  - Affected file: ~/bin/nexus-notifier.sh + nx/deploy/nexus-notifier.sh (after this fix lands)

title: Extend /hooks handler to persist events into dashboards
description:
Context: CC hooks now successfully deliver events to nexus via http://localhost:7400/hooks (migration landed 2026-04-24 from stale unix socket path). The /hooks HTTP handler at apps/agent/src/routes/hooks.ts currently only logs events via pino and returns 200 ack — it does not persist, materialize dashboards, or fire notifications. Prior comment referenced a 'socket dispatch layer' for lifecycle management; no such layer exists.

What needs to happen:
- Parse HookEventPayload events into session_events / health_snapshots / equivalent tables (extend @nexus/db schema if needed)
- Trigger notifications on relevant events (tool_use_fail, session_stop with crash, permission_request)
- Emit to WebSocket subscribers for live dashboard updates
- Handle the 20+ event_types defined in ~/.claude/scripts/hooks/telemetry.sh (nexus currently recognizes 6, falls through to unknown for the rest)

Known event types coming in:
  Lifecycle: session_start, session_stop, session_summary, session_heartbeat, session_terminate, post_compact, pre_compact
  Agents: agent_spawn, agent_telemetry, agent_complete
  Tools: tool_use_end, tool_use_fail
  Commands: command_start, command_end, user_prompt
  Other: permission_request, teammate_idle, task_completed, instructions_loaded, config_change, worktree_create, worktree_remove, notification, hook_failure

Pointers:
  - handler: apps/agent/src/routes/hooks.ts
  - event schema in CC: ~/.claude/scripts/hooks/telemetry.sh (search 'json_event')
  - payload type: HookEventPayload interface in hooks.ts (needs expansion)

Event destination routing policy in CC (reference only, not a nexus concern):
  - All events → nexus (general event sink)
  - Curated subset → Sentry (tool_use_fail, session_stop crash, session_summary, command_end error, permission_request, hook_failure)
notes: Filed from cc /workflow:evolve follow-up on 2026-04-24. Triggering incident: nx_send calls in telemetry.sh were silent no-ops for unknown duration because nx-send.sh targeted /tmp/nexus-agent.sock which never existed. After migration to HTTP, the full event stream now reaches nexus — but handler is only ack. Extension unblocks dashboard value that the hooks pipeline was always intended to support.

[SPEC] split-core-browser-barrel
Split @nexus/core barrel to isolate Node-only modules from client code
description: The client component apps/nextjs/src/app/specs/spec-events-subscriber.tsx broke the nextjs build because @nexus/core's root barrel re-exports Node-only helpers (safeSpawn, expandTilde, parseConfig) that transitively pull node:path/node:os. Webpack cannot resolve node: schemes for the browser bundle. Fix today inlined a frame parser as a workaround (commit 6a4be9e). Proper fix: split packages/core/package.json exports to have a browser-safe subpath (e.g. @nexus/core/wire) carrying only zod schemas and types, and keep node-only helpers under the default barrel or a @nexus/core/node subpath. Without this, the next client-side consumer of a core type will trip the same build failure and silently serve stale .next/ via systemd.
